title: Axum
subtitle: Axum is the HTTP layer under most of my Rust services: the memory gateway, the voice engine's control surface, the execution substrate's endpoints.

stats.label: REST endpoints in FAFOHive's API, beside its MCP transport
lines in Helix's WebSocket endpoint for media frames
timeout for the code-path explainer, one of the per-tool limits

lede: FAFOHive is one Rust process that every managed agent seat in my estate connects to, and Axum is its HTTP layer. It serves the MCP transport and a REST API. The MCP transport started on the rmcp SDK's streaming server-sent-events service, and that service broke whenever a container restarted. Container restarts are routine in my estate, so I replaced it with a per-request, TLS-terminated POST handler in Axum. Long-running tools get their own timeouts, sized to what each tool does, so one slow tool cannot hold a connection open indefinitely. FAFO Core and Function Forge needed a gateway that turns any generated function into an agent-callable tool without someone editing a router by hand.
quote: My work with Axum is in transport choice, routing and middleware structure.
evidence: Rust web services with Axum: the HTTP layer of an MCP server with ~70 REST endpoints in a 19,000-line API module, beside the MCP transport.
MCP server design: a streaming transport that broke on container restart replaced with a per-request, TLS-terminated POST handler, with per-tool timeouts such as 2 min for the code-path explainer.
API gateway design: a gateway whose MCP tool routes are generated from YAML at build time, with authentication applied as middleware per route group so new handlers inherit it.
author: Corey James
